basic_info.title: Think2Drive: Efficient Reinforcement Learning by Thinking in Latent World Model for Quasi-Realistic Autonomous Driving (in CARLA-v2)
basic_info.authors: Qifeng Li, Xiaosong Jia, Shaobo Wang, Junchi Yan (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
basic_info.code_available: no (no official code release found; related benchmark Bench2Drive/CornerCase-Repository at https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2Drive)

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Think2Drive directly inspires the latent-world-model RL pillar (a DreamerV3-style compact latent world model acting as a neural simulator in which the planner is trained), but it is a model-based RL driving planner in the CARLA-v2 simulator, not a GPS map-matching method. It learns from simulated AD state/BEV observations and outputs low-level control, never ingesting raw fleet GPS and never performing GPS-to-road matching.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination_note: Real gap: latent-world-model RL has not been applied to sequential road-segment selection / GPS map matching.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Architectural inspiration only (cited directly in the thesis hypothesis for latent-space RL decisions); it operates on AD simulator control, not BMW fleet GPS analytics or map matching.
